details.summary: This is an exemplary recipe for the cookbook. It perfectly balances the nutritional constraints, maximizes flavor, incorporates accessible convenience items like microwavable brown rice, and easily hits the 30-minute weeknight promise.

dimensions.feedback: The flavor profile is well-balanced. The acidity of the tomatoes and yogurt complements the sweetness of the peas and the warmth of the curry powder. Using Greek yogurt as a finishing touch mimics heavy cream effectively.
Every listed ingredient is used properly in the instructions, and no surprise ingredients appear.
Instructions are extremely thorough. Time ranges are provided, minimum check times are noted, doneness cues are clear, and stirring the nonfat yogurt in off-heat prevents curdling.
Perfectly aligns with an everyday Indian-American profile using accessible pantry staples.
A quick skillet simmer is the ideal method here. Taking the pan off the heat before adding the yogurt is a crucial, correctly executed step.
The computed nutrition aligns perfectly with the ingredient amounts. The combination of peas and brown rice easily accounts for the high fiber and complex carbohydrate counts.
The title and intro accurately reflect the dish without any banned health claims or scare tactics.
Highly appealing. It's a quick, colorful, comforting, and hearty weeknight dinner that looks good in a bowl.
Nails the dual-condition brief perfectly: relies on lean protein, high-quality fiber-rich carbohydrates, olive oil, and loads of vegetables/legumes without heavy fats.
Carbohydrates hit the target window beautifully (45.6 g) using whole brown rice and peas. There is zero added sugar, strictly adhering to the book's core tenet.
Fits the 'Chicken, Turkey & Lean Meat Dinners' chapter effortlessly. It hits all nutrient targets and uses an approved lean poultry cut.
Easily achievable in under 30 minutes from start to finish. The use of a ready-to-eat brown rice pouch is a smart, explicitly permitted shortcut that honors the reader's time.
